nodes.description: Missense variants alter TUBB8, a primate-specific beta-tubulin expressed almost exclusively in oocytes and the early embryo, where it constitutes nearly all expressed beta-tubulin. There is no redundancy to fall back on, which is why a heterozygous missense variant is sufficient and why the phenotype is confined to the oocyte. The variants affect chaperone-dependent folding and assembly of the alpha/beta-tubulin heterodimer, disrupt microtubule behaviour in cultured cells, and alter microtubule dynamics in vivo. The founding study characterises the effects as dominant-negative.

genetic_context.description: Heterozygous missense variants acting dominant-negatively - stated directly by the founding study, and consistent with the mechanism: a mutant subunit that folds poorly or incorporates aberrantly degrades a beta-tubulin pool that has no other isotype to compensate it in this cell type.

nodes.description: Primary infertility due to oocyte maturation arrest. Affected women are otherwise healthy - the restricted expression of TUBB8 means there is no somatic phenotype - and the infertility is not overcome by standard assisted reproduction, because the defect is in the oocyte rather than in fertilization.

nodes.description: A mechanistically targeted rescue, preclinical and variant-specific. In TUBB8-D417N oocytes the spindle loses stable acetylated microtubules and accumulates HDAC6, the deacetylase that removes the stabilizing modification. Culturing those oocytes with the selective HDAC6 inhibitors tubacin or tubastatin A restored morphologically normal spindles and drastically recovered the polar-body extrusion rate - meaning the arrest itself was relieved, not merely a marker. This has not been tested in humans, and the authors are explicit that it addresses a certain group of TUBB8-mutated patients rather than all of them.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic variants of TUBB8 cause oocyte spindle defects by disrupting with EB1/CAKP5 interactions and potential treatment targeting microtubule acetylation through HDAC6 inhibition.
evidence.snippet: These rescue results shed light on the strategy to treat meiotic defects in a certain group of TUBB8 mutated patients.

nodes.description: The cellular failure, and the level at which the disease has recently been resolved further. Reduction of the tubulin dimer pool is the main etiology but does not explain many variants. For those, the defect is in nucleation: mutant TUBB8 depletes the EB1 plus-end signal, diminishes the affinity of EB1 for microtubules, and impairs the microtubule interaction with CKAP5/TACC3 - both required to initiate nucleation - with an attenuated Ran-GTP pathway downstream. The spindle that results is not merely small but unstable: acetylated, stable microtubules are largely abolished and HDAC6 accumulates.

nodes.description: The disease-defining event. Oocytes resume meiosis but arrest at metaphase I, failing to extrude the first polar body and never reaching the fertilizable metaphase II state. Because the arrest is in the oocyte itself, it is not bypassed by intracytoplasmic sperm injection.
